title: Gratitude That Returns to Naam
subtitle: Mundhaavanee Fifth Mehl
summary: This short shalok is a mature form of gratitude. It does not begin in self-congratulation but in humility, mercy, and the gift of Naam.
whyItMatters: It helps gratitude move past positivity into truthful dependence on grace.
takeaway: Real gratitude does not inflate the self. It softens it.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਤੋ ਨਾਹੀ ਮੈਨੋ ਜੋਗੁ ਕੀਤੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: teraa keetaa jaato naahee maino jog keetoiee ||
lines.translation: I have not appreciated what You have done for me, Lord; only You can make me worthy.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੈ ਨਿਰਗੁਣਿਆਰੇ ਕੋ ਗੁਣੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਆਪੇ ਤਰਸੁ ਪਇਓਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: mai niraguniaare ko gun naahee aape taras pioiee ||
lines.translation: I am unworthy - I have no worth or virtues at all. You have taken pity on me.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਰਸੁ ਪਇਆ ਮਿਹਰਾਮਤਿ ਹੋਈ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਸਜਣੁ ਮਿਲਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: taras piaa miharaamat hoiee satigur sajan miliaa ||
lines.translation: You took pity on me, and blessed me with Your Mercy, and I have met the True Guru, my Friend.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਤਾਂ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਤਨੁ ਮਨੁ ਥੀਵੈ ਹਰਿਆ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak naam milai taa(n) jeevaa(n) tan man theevai hariaa ||1||
lines.translation: O Nanak, if I am blessed with the Naam, I live, and my body and mind blossom forth. ||1||

structure: Begins by admitting that the Lord's care has not been properly appreciated.
Moves through unworthiness and mercy rather than self-esteem.
Ends by locating life itself in the gift of Naam.

evidence.coreClaim: This short shalok is a mature form of gratitude. It does not begin in self-congratulation but in humility, mercy, and the gift of Naam.
evidence.turn: Moves through unworthiness and mercy rather than self-esteem.
evidence.practicalImplication: Real gratitude does not inflate the self. It softens it.
